extracted.intended_audience: researchers, stakeholders, OMB reviewers, and public commenters on NHTSA information collections
extracted.subtask_short: PRA ICR: motorcycle safety gear study
extracted.subtask_description: Notice of an Information Collection Request (ICR) submitted to OMB under the Paperwork Reduction Act seeking approval for a one-time survey of motorcyclists to assess fit, comfort, and perceived protective value of motorcycle gear. The notice describes sample size, recruitment, measurement methods, burden estimates, data uses, and requests public comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB approval requirement under the PRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PRA (44 U.S.C. 3501 et seq.), a Federal agency must receive approval from the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) before it collects certain information from the public and a person is not required to respond to a collection of information by a Federal agency unless the collection displays a valid OMB control number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice announces that the following information collection request will be submitted to OMB for review and approval; the ICR describes the nature of the information collection and its expected burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary and anonymous participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation will be voluntary and anonymous. Participants will not report personally identifiable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no record-keeping costs to participants; participants will incur no burden related to annual reporting or record keeping due to the collection of this new information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and screening targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Targeted sample of 625 motorcycle riders, from 1,250 screened for potential participation (expected to contact approximately 1,250 motorcyclists at data collection locations to obtain 625 responses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect 125 respondents from each of five motorcycle types (standard, cruiser, sport, adventure/touring, seated motor scooter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal representation by motorcycle type
rubrics_metrics.description: The study protocol calls for the recruitment of an equal number of riders of standard, cruiser, sport and adventure/touring motorcycles, and seated motor scooters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan recruitment at venues and times to achieve roughly 125 participants per type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment locations and approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential participants will be recruited at locations where riders gather, such as rallies, training events, and other organized social events; study team will either invite riders to participate at a study tent or conduct the survey near the rider's motorcycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recruitment approach is not limited to rallies; comment response explains recruitment includes other events to broaden sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: One gear type assessed per participant
rubrics_metrics.description: The study plan is to assess one type of protective gear (e.g., jackets) per participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain perspectives on different gear types, staff will present images of protective gear (one gear type per participant) that ranges in quality; images include product descriptions but no brand names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection modes and instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a portable tablet for the informed consent process and to record participant responses and staff observations; participants self-administer some portions; data collectors verbally ask participants during gear assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms used: NHTSA Forms 2000 (Informed Consent/Screener) and Forms 2001–2005 (gear-specific forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective fit assessment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Study staff will observe gear worn by riders, assess the fit of the gear, and take anthropometric measurements (e.g., head circumference) using ribbon tape or an anthropometer as appropriate depending on gear type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments combine staff observations, objective measurements, and participant perceptions to allow comparison of perceived vs. objectively measured fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of images without brand identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Study staff will present images on a tablet of protective gear (one gear type per participant) that ranges in quality; the images will include product descriptions, but no brand names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images used to obtain participants' ratings of protection, quality, and likelihood of wearing/purchasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study purpose and expected uses of data
rubrics_metrics.description: NHTSA will use the information to assess the relationship between perceived and objectively measured fit, understand rider beliefs about protective value of gear that influence selection and use, and to develop programs to improve motorcyclist safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results will be used to produce a technical report with summary statistics and tables; a de-identified data set will be made publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: No personally identifiable information collected; public de-identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants will not report personally identifiable information. A de-identified data set will also be made available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is anonymous; ensure any public dataset is de-identified before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and instrument mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Form Numbers: NHTSA Forms 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005. Form 2000 is the Informed Consent/Screener; Forms 2001–2005 correspond to footwear, gloves, helmets, jackets, pants respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden per form and number of responses are detailed in tables; staff should administer the appropriate form depending on gear assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden estimates (time and hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated total annual burden hours: 341 hours. Breakdown: 313 hours for 625 full participants (30 minutes each), 19 hours for 75 partial participants (15 minutes each), 9 hours for 550 screened but non-participating individuals (1 minute each).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables provide minutes per respondent by participation type and form; numbers rounded to nearest hour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated burden cost and wage assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Total burden cost to participants is estimated at $14,460 with an annual burden cost of $4,820 (total divided by 3). Average hourly opportunity cost used: $42.46 inclusive of a 30% fringe ($32.66 base wage + $9.80 fringe).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs calculated per form and aggregated; rounding applied as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency and approval length requested
rubrics_metrics.description: This study will be a one-time data collection. Length of approval requested: 3 years from date of approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because data collection may occur at multiple events there is remote chance of duplicate participation; not expected as locations/times not publicly known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent process requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Form 2000 for informed consent/screener; Form 2000 takes approximately 1 minute per contacted individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 2000 is administered to all screened individuals (including those who decline further participation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment screening and nonparticipant accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate of screened but nonparticipating individuals: 550 people screened and decline to participate; screening interaction estimated at 1 minute each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include screening interactions in total burden calculations and account for partial participants separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment solicitation topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comments invited on: (i) whether the proposed collection is necessary and has practical utility; (ii) accuracy of the burden estimate; (iii) ways to enhance quality, utility and clarity of information to be collected; and (iv) ways to minimize burden, including automated techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be received by the stated close date and submitted via reginfo.gov to find the ICR under review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limits and responses to substantive comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency responses to comments clarify scope: e.g., declines to expand the study to explore crash outcomes because that is beyond current study scope; recruitment is broader than rallies to include training events and other organized events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and adhere to study scope; explain reasons for not expanding scope when responding to comments.
